title: IonQ Secures $7.5 Million Phase 2 AFRL Allocation to Expand Rome, NY Quantum Network with Free-Space Optics and Frequency Conversion - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IonQ received a $7.5M Phase 2 AFRL allocation to upgrade its Rome, NY quantum network with free-space optics, quantum frequency converters and automation software, under a $21.1M multi-year collaboration inherited via its Qubitekk acquisition.

insights.claim: IonQ received a $7.5 million Phase 2 follow-on allocation from the Air Force Research Laboratory to expand its Rome, New York quantum networking installation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Incremental defense revenue and validation for IonQ's networking unit.

insights.claim: The Phase 2 allocation exercises planned options under a broader $21.1 million multi-year collaboration initiated after IonQ acquired quantum networking specialist Qubitekk.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows the Qubitekk acquisition is generating contract flow.

insights.claim: The contract complements a $54.5 million computing and networking research agreement signed with AFRL in 2024, an on-site trapped-ion system at Rome, and a first remote photonic interconnect demonstration under DARPA's HARQ program.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IonQ has a layered, growing defense relationship worth tracking in backlog.
insights.locator: The contract expands on a series of joint milestones

insights.claim: Phase 2 adds C-band free-space optical transceivers with Pointing, Acquisition and Tracking to route entanglement over line-of-sight open-air paths for terrestrial and mobile tactical nodes.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Free-space links are a step toward mobile and satellite-compatible defense quantum networks.

insights.claim: Dual Quantum Frequency Converter modules translate native trapped-ion emission wavelengths into standard telecom C- and O-bands to link heterogeneous quantum devices.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Frequency conversion is the key enabling component for networking across modalities.

insights.claim: The upgrade also includes upgraded Quantum NICs with active polarization controllers and on-premises autonomous orchestration software for self-tests, dynamic route failover, link monitoring and data logging.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Control-plane automation indicates a move toward operational, not lab, networks.

insights.claim: Trapped-ion systems emit photons at atomic transition wavelengths that suffer severe attenuation in standard telecom fiber or the atmosphere, making the interface between hardware modalities and long-haul lines a primary bottleneck for distributed quantum architectures.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Wavelength conversion is a gating technology for distributed quantum computing.
insights.locator: Bridging Closed Cryostats to Open Tactical Channels

insights.claim: By maintaining entanglement routing over open-air paths, AFRL aims to evaluate quantum communication protocols in tactical scenarios where fixed fiber is unavailable.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Defense customers are driving demand for field-deployable quantum networking.
insights.locator: Simultaneously, the integration of free-space optics
